title: STUDY TO FIND OUT WHETHER A SHORTER ANTIBIOTIC TREATMENT (7 DAYS) IS AS EFFECTIVE AND SAFE AS THE USUAL ONE (14 DAYS) IN PATIENTS WITH AN INFECTION IN THEIR TRANSPLANTED KIDNEY (KTI)
official: Prospective Multicenter Randomized Non-Inferiority Study Comparing 7 Days Versus 14 Days of Antibiotic Treatment for Graft Pyelonephritis in Kidney Transplant Recipients (KTI)
summary: Main objective: The primary objective of the study is to demonstrate the non-inferiority of a 7-day treatment regimen compared to 14 days of antibiotic treatments used in usual clinical practice in patients with graft pyelonephritis.
conditions: Graft pyelonephritis in kidney transplant recipients
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adult kidney transplant recipients ≥ 18 years of age, of both sexes, who experience an episode of acute graft pyelonephritis at any time from the transplant to 48 hours after the start of antibiotic treatment.
2. Patients must be willing and able to provide written informed consent for the trial. If a subject is unable to provide written informed consent independently, a legal representative may do so in their place.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Clinical instability 48 hours after the start of antibiotic treatment due to an episode of acute graft pyelonephritis defined as: hypotension, anuria, fever equal to or greater than 38ºC, need for vasopressor drugs or admission to the intensive care unit.
2. Pregnant or breastfeeding patients.
3. Patients with known anatomical alterations that predispose to urinary tract infections (such as vesicoureteral reflux or obstructive prostatic hypertrophy).
4. Presence of urinary catheters such as bladder catheters or ureteral catheters.
5. Presence of complications such as urinary obstruction or kidney abscess.
6. Kidney transplant recipients admitted for an episode of graft pyelonephritis in the previous 30 days.
7. Participation in another clinical trial in which the protocol establishes antibiotic treatment for pyelonephritis.
8. Previous inclusion in the present study.
9. No authorization from the patient or their legal representative to sign the informed consent.
10. Any medical, psychiatric, or family condition that, in the investigator's judgment, could jeopardize or compromise the patient's ability to participate in the study.
